claims.text: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a lamellar FCC/B2 dual-phase structure.
The FCC phase is enriched in Co, Cr, and Fe, whereas the B2 phase is enriched in Ni and Al.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy exhibits high room-temperature ductility and strength.
Aging near 600°C forms highly ordered, Ni3Al-like L12 domains within the FCC matrix.
Aging near 600°C produces or enhances jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries.
Strong chemical ordering raises the energetic cost of creating antiphase boundaries during dislocation motion.
Near-stoichiometric Ni3Al-like ordering in the FCC phase creates high APBE in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
High APBE inhibits cross-slip of screw dislocations.
Jagged B2/FCC boundaries geometrically constrain dislocation motion.
The combination of high APBE and jagged boundaries forces planar slip.
Planar slip produces localized stress concentrations at boundary serrations that cause brittle fracture.
Increasing the aging temperature to about 750°C decreases the degree of chemical order and its associated dislocation resistance.
Reduced ordering at about 750°C lowers APBE and restores cross-slip.
Aging near 750°C smooths the phase boundaries or forms ductile transition zones along them.
Aging at 600°C causes a substantial loss of elongation, while aging at 750°C restores ductility.
The 600°C-aged state will have greater nanoindentation hardness than the 750°C-aged state.
The 600°C-aged state will exhibit smaller displacement bursts during nanoindentation than the 750°C-aged state.
The ductile transition occurs when the FCC chemical-order parameter falls below a threshold at which APBE can no longer suppress cross-slip under the constraint of jagged boundaries.
Sigma-phase decomposition is not observed in the specific 600°C brittle window.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes the brittle window as extending through 750°C and places the transition to ductility above 750°C, whereas the predicted outcome and baseline classify the material aged at 750°C itself as ductile.
